prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 1997 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: “Yes We Can” make Scotland wealthier, fairer and better governed through independence, using Scotland’s resources for Scotland’s priorities.

Case for independence:
- Scotland is a wealthy net contributor to the UK; with North Sea revenues it would rank among the richest nations.
- Independence would bring full EU membership, open borders with England, protected pensions/investments, and citizenship based on birth or residency.
- Route: Elect a majority of SNP MPs → negotiate with UK and EU (6–12 months) → referendum on the independence settlement → formal independence → new election.

Constitution and governance:
- Written constitution and Bill of Rights guaranteeing civil, social and economic rights (including free health care, education, minimum wage).
- Single-chamber parliament elected by proportional representation; votes at 16; strong committee oversight; reformed monarchy; entrenched local government (also PR).

Economy, jobs and tax:
- Aim for full employment; 100,000 new jobs; National Apprenticeship scheme; Skills Foundation; Export Unit; doubled tourism marketing; R&D boost.
- Business tax cuts: corporation tax to 30p; small companies to 18p; abolish Class IV NICs; fair trading and prompt payment rules.
- Social partnership: adopt EU Social Chapter; Charter for Trade Union Rights; minimum wage at half median male earnings.
- Personal tax: introduce 15p starter rate; widen basic-rate band; remove NI ceiling so top earners contribute more; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%.

Social justice, health and safety:
- Child Benefit to £12.50; restore benefits for 16–17s.
- Pensioners’ package: weekly pension rise (+£3 single/+£5 couples), Cold Climate Allowance, remove standing charges for utilities, end means-testing for residential care.
- NHS: scrap internal market; national and local Health Commissions; +£35m/year; reintegrate dentistry; fairer prescriptions; ban tobacco ads and raise tobacco duty; strong food safety agency.
- Crime: support “zero tolerance” for community crime; more police resources; vehicle register to curb fraud; expand community sentences and rehabilitation; total handgun ban and full Cullen implementation.

Education, housing, local services, culture:
- Hire 700 teachers; repair schools; internet access in every school; free nursery for all 3–4s; restore student grants; expand quality training places; support Gaelic/Scots and community language needs.
- Housing: transfer 75% of council housing debt to unlock £1.6bn; build 20,000 affordable homes; upgrade substandard and damp homes; protect new/improved stock from discounted right-to-buy; replace Scottish Homes with an accountable agency.
- Local government: restore powers from quangos; reform finance and move toward local income tax; abolish water quangos.
- Culture: create Scottish Broadcasting Corporation (public service) plus diverse commercial outlets; Scottish Screen; equal legal status for Gaelic and Scots; launch “Scot-Lot” lottery (no scratch cards).

Land, rural economy, environment, energy, transport, telecoms:
- Abolish feudal tenure; Land Commission; public land register; local control of foreshore/seabed; improved access.
- Agriculture: BSE traceability; CAP reform; diversification; market access; strong food standards.
- Fisheries: regional management, conservation, fair enforcement, processing support (+£10m/year).
- Forestry: National Forest Enterprise Board; double woodland in 25 years, focusing on native species.
- End nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; pivot to clean-up and renewables R&D.
- Energy: claim North Sea resources via established legal demarcation; stable regime; end gas “landing” discrimination; phase out nuclear; invest in renewables and efficiency; reassess deep coal.
- Transport: invest in rail and electrification; integrate buses; remove Skye Bridge tolls (shadow tolls then public ownership); strengthen ferries; fairer air duty for remote areas; expand direct flights.
- Telecoms: stronger regulation and rural rollout; distance learning; incentives for teleworking; promote internet access; protect users via ratings and anti-fraud law (no new censorship).

Europe, world and defence:
- Full EU membership with vote/veto; focus on better CFP and CAP; maximise EU funds; democratic EU representation.
- Targeted diplomatic network serving trade and citizens; active roles in UN, Council of Europe, Commonwealth; cooperative British Isles forum.
- Scottish Defence Forces (army, navy, air force) at existing bases; peacekeeping college; remove Trident; phased NATO withdrawal while cooperating via other frameworks; defence diversification and procurement anchored in Scotland.

Paying for it:
- Fully costed 4-year budget: reorders spending (e.g., Trident savings), uses Scotland’s fiscal surplus, models growth effects, and dedicates £6.6bn to debt repayment while funding enterprise, tax reforms, education, health and social justice.
